references.text: The preceding verse in the context where Jesus speaks of those considered worthy to attain the coming world and the resurrection from the dead, see [ref:Luk 20:35|Luke 20:35].
John writes that we shall be like him when he appears, pointing toward the transformed state of the resurrected, being like angels – [ref:1 Joh 3:2|1 John 3:2].
Jesus' parallel statement in Matthew that in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like God's angels in heaven – [ref:Matt 22:30|Matthew 22:30].
Mark's parallel passage where Jesus says that when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven – [ref:Mark 12:25|Mark 12:25].
Paul writes that all who are led by God's Spirit are children of God (υἱοὶ θεοῦ), connecting to the expression "sons of God" used for the resurrected in [ref:Rom 8:14|Romans 8:14].
Paul refers to the fulfillment of adoption as the redemption of our bodies, namely the coming resurrection when believers are fully revealed as children of God – [ref:Rom 8:23|Romans 8:23].
Paul writes that Christ will transform our lowly body to be like his glorious body, describing the transformed state of the resurrected – [ref:Fil 3:21|Philippians 3:21].
Paul's teaching on the resurrection body: what is sown in perishability is raised in imperishability; the resurrected can no longer die – [ref:1 Kor 15:42-44|1 Corinthians 15:42-44].
Believers will bear the image of the heavenly Adam in the resurrection, a transformation that means death no longer has power – [ref:1 Kor 15:49|1 Corinthians 15:49].
In the new existence, death will be no more, corresponding to the fact that the resurrected can no longer die – [ref:Åp 21:4|Revelation 21:4].

Paul states that Christ, raised from the dead, dies no more; death has no longer dominion over him. This principle also applies to believers united with him in the resurrection – [ref:Rom 6:9|Romans 6:9].
Elihu speaks of angels (sons of God) and their closeness to God, providing background for the expression "like angels" (ἰσάγγελοι) – [ref:Job 36:29|Job 36:29].
In Luke's genealogy, Adam is called "son of God", showing that the expression "sons of God" (υἱοὶ θεοῦ) refers to those whose life comes directly from God – [ref:Luk 3:38|Luke 3:38].
